title: Eventual cohomology stabilization gives stalk injectivity for a derived limit
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, let $x\in X$ and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose there are an index $n(x)$ and a fundamental system $\mathfrak U_x$ of open neighborhoods of $x$ such that, for every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$, (i) $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)=0$, and (ii) for every $n\ge n(x)$ the transition map $H^m(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ is injective. Then the natural map on stalks $H^m(R\varprojlim_n K_n)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ is injective. Here cohomology is sheaf cohomology on opens [pqf-def-cohomology] and the derived limit is as in [def-weil-derived-limit].
